IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p178/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p178/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p178/r7.claim: A singular speaker can be addressed in the plural; kings conventionally say “we” for themselves, and scripture mirrors their usage.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p178/r7.anchor: ومنه أن يخاطب الواحد بلفظ الجميع:

BURHAN:v2p234/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p234/r6.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v2p234/r6.claim: Some take ارجعون as ارجعني, a singular addressing himself in the plural out of self-aggrandizement, as in the speaker’s use of “we.”
BURHAN:v2p234/r6.anchor: وجعل منه بعضهم قوله تعالى ﴿ قال رب ارجعون ﴾ أي ارجعني

BURHAN:v2p234/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p234/r7.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p234/r7.claim: Another view takes رب as a cry for help and ارجعون as plural address to the angels, or as repeated speech like قفا نبك.
BURHAN:v2p234/r7.anchor: وقيل ﴿ رب ﴾ استغاثة و ﴿ ارجعون ﴾ خطاب الملائكة

BURHAN:v2p234/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p234/r8.speaker: السهيلي
BURHAN:v2p234/r8.claim: Al-Suhaylī says the dying person is confused by devils and punishment guards and blurts out his habitual worldly appeal to created beings.
BURHAN:v2p234/r8.anchor: وقال السهيلي هو قول من حضرته الشياطين وزبانية العذاب فاختلط

BURSEVI:v6p74#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p74#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p74#3/r1.claim: The introductory حتى begins a sentence but also marks the endpoint of the preceding account: the unbelievers persist in false claims until death, when the afterlife becomes visible.
BURSEVI:v6p74#3/r1.anchor: حتى التي يبتدأ بها الكلام دخلت على الجملة الاسمية وهي مع ذلك غاية

BURSEVI:v6p74#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p74#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p74#3/r2.claim: At irreversible death, the unbeliever regrets neglecting faith and deeds and begs to be returned.
BURSEVI:v6p74#3/r2.anchor: تحسرا على ما فرط فيه من الإيمان والعمل

BURSEVI:v6p74#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p74#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p74#3/r3.claim: The plural waw in ارجعون honors a singular addressee; the author rejects the claim that such honorific plural address occurs only in later Arabic.
BURSEVI:v6p74#3/r3.anchor: والواو لتعظيم المخاطب لأن العرب تخاطب الواحد الجليل الشأن بلفظ الجماعة

QIRAAT-ER:23:99:8#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:23:99:8#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:23:99:8#1/r1.claim: Ten-reader recitations retain the full first-person object-pronoun yāʾ.
QIRAAT-ER:23:99:8#1/r1.anchor: Full yāʾ retained (irjiʿūnī vs. irjiʿūni) — 10-reader recitations preserve the 1s object pronoun yāʾ in full

QUSHAYRI:v2p350/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p350/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p350/r8.claim: At death, when distress has seized them and escape is impossible, people plead and submit; they are told they should have done so earlier.
QUSHAYRI:v2p350/r8.anchor: إذ أخذ البلاء بخناقهم ، واستمكن الضر من أحوالهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p350/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p350/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p350/r9.claim: A poem urges the soul to return before the road is blocked.

SULAMI:v2p39/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p39/r1.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v2p39/r1.claim: If the damned knew what deeds could save them, they would plead to return and act righteously; obey God now, avoid spiritual claims, and correct one's practice, since abandoning the path leaves one stalled.
SULAMI:v2p39/r1.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : في كتاب له إلى أهل جوزجان لو علم أهل النار عملا أنجا لهم في طاعة الله ، والصلاح لما فرغوا في وقت العيان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p582/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p582/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p582/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī connects “until death comes” to the disbelievers' continued bad speech, taking the intervening prayer as a parenthetical appeal for divine help against satanic provocation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p582/r9.anchor: حتى يتعلق بيصفون أي لا يزالون على سوء الذكر إلى هذا الوقت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p582/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p582/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p582/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya treats ḥattā as an opening particle, possibly marking an endpoint with omitted words; the author objects that even an opening ḥattā retains endpoint force and Ibn ʿAṭiyya leaves the omission unexplained.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p582/r10.anchor: حتى في هذا الموضع حرف ابتداء، ويحتمل أن تكون غاية مجردة بتقدير كلام محذوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p582/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p582/r11.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p582/r11.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ says ḥattā marks an endpoint in a sense like coordination; the author's own reconstruction supplies an omitted clause: the Prophet will not be like disbelievers attended by satans until death.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p582/r11.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء حتى غاية في معنى العطف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p583/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p583/r1.speaker: القشيري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p583/r1.claim: Al-Qushayrī says the disbelievers persist in denial despite God's proofs until death brings certainty, sight of the angels, and useless regret.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p583/r1.anchor: وقال القشيري: احتج تعالى عليهم وذكرهم قدرته ثم قال: مصرون على الإنكار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p583/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p583/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p583/r2.claim: The plural in “return me” may reverentially address God as a plural, or the dying person may first appeal to God and then call the punishment angels; Ibn Jurayj gives the latter explanation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p583/r2.anchor: وإما استغاث أولا بربه وخاطب ملائكة العذاب وقاله ابن جريج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p583/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p583/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p583/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says one who failed to pay alms and perform pilgrimage asks to return; others object that the verse concerns disbelievers and cite the call to spend in 63:10. Al-Awzāʿī identifies the asker as one who withheld alms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p583/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: من لم يزك ولم يحج سأل الرجعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p583/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p583/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p583/r4.claim: When death arrives and the person sees it, he asks to return to worldly life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p583/r4.anchor: وجاء الموت أي حضر وعاينه الإنسان فحينئذ يسأل الرجعة إلى الدنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p583/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p583/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p583/r5.claim: A hadith contrasts the believer, who declines return to the home of sorrows and goes on to God, with the disbeliever, who asks to return and do good.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p583/r5.anchor: إذا عاين المؤمن الموت قالت له الملائكة: نرجعك فيقول إلى دار الهموم والأحزان

ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r1.claim: Here ḥattā begins a sentence and marks the endpoint of an omitted prior clause; the ‘even Kalīb insults me’ example leaves the statement that everyone insults the speaker implicit.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r1.anchor: ابتدائية وغاية لمقدر يدل عليه ما قبلها والتقدير فلا أكون كالكفار

ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r2.claim: Alternatively it attaches to the second ‘they describe,’ making slander last until death; ‘say, Lord’ interrupts to urge protection from Satan and obedience to repel evil graciously.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r2.anchor: حتى متعلقة بمحذوف يدل عليه كأنه قيل : لا يزالون على سوء المقالة والطعن

ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r3.claim: Attaching ḥattā to the first ‘they describe’ or to ‘they associate partners’ is judged untenable.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r3.anchor: على ( يصفون ) الأول أو على ( يشركون ) وليس بشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī links the passage to ‘they are liars’: denying God a son through this point interrupts the discourse to establish their lies and deserved punishment; al-Ālūsī rejects it.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r4.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري أن يكون مرورا على قوله تعالى ( وإنهم لكاذبون )

ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya allows ḥattā to begin a sentence without endpoint force; Abū Ḥayyān objects that it necessarily retains endpoint meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r5.anchor: من كلام ابن عطية أنه يجوز أن تكون ( حتى ) هنا ابتدائية لا غاية

ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r6.claim: The pronoun ‘one of them’ refers to unbelievers; death’s arrival means signs of death and conditions of the next life appear.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r6.anchor: أن ضمير ( أحدهم ) راجع إلى الكفار والمراد من مجيء الموت ظهور أماراته

ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r7.claim: The plural imperative ‘return me’ may honor God, as poetry shows one person addressed in plural; the author rejects denial of this usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r7.anchor: والواو لتعظيم المخاطب وهو الله تعالى كما في قوله : ألا فاحموني يا إله محمد

ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r8.claim: Alternatively, the plural addresses angels, with ‘my Lord’s angels’ understood, or ‘Lord’ invokes God while ‘return me’ addresses angels.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r8.anchor: وقيل : الواو لكون الخطاب للملائكة عليهم السلام والكلام على تقدير مضاف

ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r9.speaker: ابن جرير عن ابن جريج
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r9.claim: A report relayed by Ibn Jurayj says believers offered return reject it as return to grief, whereas unbelievers ask God to send them back.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r9.anchor: أخرجه ابن جرير وابن المنذر عن ابن جرير قال : زعموا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r10.speaker: المازني
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r10.claim: Al-Māzinī says the plural pronoun signals repeated pleading, so ‘return me’ means it three times; he compares the dual in qifā nabki.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p62#3/r10.anchor: جمع الضمير ليدل على التكرار فكأنه قال : رب أرجعني أرجعني أرجعني

ALUSI-FULL:v18p63/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p63/r1.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v18p63/r1.claim: Al-Khafājī objects that the singular imperative’s underlying form contains no plural pronoun, leaving al-Māzinī’s metaphor unexplained.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p63/r1.anchor: واستشكل ذلك الخفاجي بأنه كان أصل ارجعوا مثلا ارجع ارجع ارجع لم يكن ضمير الجمع

ALUSI-FULL:v18p63/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p63/r2.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v18p63/r2.claim: Al-Khafājī proposes substituting one word-form for another without regard to meaning, letting the plural pronoun signal repetition for emphasis.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p63/r2.anchor: استعارة لفظ مكان لفظ آخر لنكتة بقطع النظر عن معناه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p63/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p63/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p63/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī says al-Khafājī went too far: plural is an honorific address to one treated as a group, making the action resemble repeated group action.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p63/r3.anchor: أراد المازني أنه جمع الضمير للتعظيم بتنزيل المخاطب الواحد منزلة الجماعة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p63/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p63/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p63/r4.claim: This explanation extends to the dual in qifā nabki only if dual address can honor one person; al-Ālūsī does not recall seeing this and leaves it open.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p63/r4.anchor: لكن إجراء نحو هذا في نحو قفا نبك لا يتسنى إلا إذا قيل بأنه قد يقصد بضمير التثنية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p428/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p428/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p428/r6.claim: Disbelievers who deny resurrection ask to return to the world when they see death.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p428/r6.anchor: يسألون الرجعة إلى الدنيا عند معاينة الموت

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p428/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p428/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p428/r7.claim: ارجعون uses an honorific plural to address God alone, as Arabs address one person in the plural.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p428/r7.anchor: فإنهم يخاطبون الواحد بلفظ الجمع على وجه التعظيم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p428/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p428/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p428/r8.claim: The plural resembles God’s own إنا نحن wording.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p428/r8.anchor: إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p428/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p428/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p428/r9.claim: An alternative is that, after appealing to God, the dying person turns to the angels taking his soul and asks them to return him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p428/r9.anchor: الملائكة الذين يقبضون روحه ابتداء بخطاب الله

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:99/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:99/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:99/r1.claim: The death clause connects with the earlier statement, with an intervening appeal to God against Satan's incitement to revenge; the dying person's plea expresses regret after seeing reality.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:99/r1.anchor: تحسرا على ما فرط فيه من الإيمان والطاعة لما اطلع على الأمر

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:99/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:99/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:99/r2.claim: The plural in return us magnifies the addressee; alternatively, it repeats the request to return, as in Arabic dual commands.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:99/r2.anchor: والواو لتعظيم المخاطب. وقيل لتكرير قوله ارجعني

NAHHAS:v3p121/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p121/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p121/r1.claim: A person may speak inwardly, as shown by the verse about people saying to themselves, ‘Why does God not punish us?’
NAHHAS:v3p121/r1.anchor: وقد يكون القول في النفس قال جل وعز ويقولون في أنفسهم لولا يعذبنا الله

NAHHAS:v3p121/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p121/r2.speaker: قول للنحويين
NAHHAS:v3p121/r2.claim: One explanation for addressing God with the plural ‘return us’ is that a ruler speaking of himself uses a plural, so others address him as a group.
NAHHAS:v3p121/r2.anchor: ففيه قولان للنحويين أحدهما أن العرب تتعارف أن الجبار إذا أخبر عن نفسه قال لنفعلن ولنرجعن

NAHHAS:v3p121/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p121/r3.speaker: المازني
NAHHAS:v3p121/r3.claim: Another view takes the plural as repeated emphasis: ‘return me’ three times, like ‘throw him into Hell’ meaning ‘throw, throw.’
NAHHAS:v3p121/r3.anchor: والقول الآخر إن معنى ارجعون على جهة التكرير ارجعن ارجعن ارجعن وهكذا قال المازني

BIQAI-FULL:v5p221/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p221/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p221/r2.claim: The greatest danger from devils comes at death, when the veil lifts and the person's fate becomes certain, so the passage warns believers to strive and pray for protection then.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p221/r2.anchor: فإنه وقت كشف الغطاء , عما كتب من القضاء , وآن اللقاء

BIQAI-FULL:v5p221/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p221/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p221/r3.claim: At death the person addresses the angels of punishment and asks to return to the world, the abode of knowledge; the plural may address God and the angels, express honorific speech to a great one, or intensify the request.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p221/r3.anchor: ويجوزأن يكون الجمع لله تعالى وللملائكة , أو للتعظيم على عادة في مخاطبات الأكابر

DURR-FULL:v6p114/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p114/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v6p114/r3.claim: A disbeliever shown his seat in the Fire asks to return and repent, but is told his lifetime has ended; his grave is constricted and its creatures torment him.
DURR-FULL:v6p114/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: إذا وضع الكافر في قبره مقعده من النار قال: {رب ارجعون} حتى أتوب أعمل صالحا

DURR-FULL:v6p114/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p114/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v6p114/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says the plea to be sent back is made before the dying person has tasted death.
DURR-FULL:v6p114/r5.anchor: عن ابن زيد في قوله {قال رب ارجعون} قال: هذا حين يعاين قبل أن يذوق الموت

DURR-FULL:v6p114/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p114/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p114/r6.claim: A report to Aisha says the believer who sees the angels refuses return to the house of sorrows and asks to go forward to God.
DURR-FULL:v6p114/r6.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال: زعموا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لعائشة إن المؤمن إذا عاين الملائكة

DURR-FULL:v6p115/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p115/r1.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v6p115/r1.claim: At death, everything that had kept a person from truth is gathered before his eyes, prompting him to ask for return so he can do good.
DURR-FULL:v6p115/r1.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اذ حضر الإنسان الوفاة يجمع له كل شيء يمنعه عن الحق

DURR-FULL:v6p115/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p115/r2.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v6p115/r2.claim: The wished-for righteous deed is to say ‘There is no god but God.’
DURR-FULL:v6p115/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله {لعلي أعمل صالحا فيما تركت} قال: لعلي أقول لا إله إلا الله

DURR-FULL:v6p115/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p115/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p115/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas likewise interprets the hoped-for good deed as saying ‘There is no god but God.’
DURR-FULL:v6p115/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {لعلي أعمل صالحا} قال: أقول لا إله إلا الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p121/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p121/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p121/r5.claim: This interpretation of the devils best suits the stated endpoint, when one of them meets death.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p121/r5.anchor: وهذا الوجه في تفسير الشياطين هو الأليق بالغاية في قوله { حتى إذا جاء أحدهم الموت }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p122/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p122/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p122/r1.claim: Ḥattā is an independent transition, not an endpoint for the preceding statement and need not attach to “they describe”; it connects instead to God’s ability to show the threatened punishment in 23:95.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p122/r1.anchor: والوجه أن ( حتى ) متصلة بقوله { وإنا على أن نريك ما نعدهم لقادرون }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p122/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p122/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p122/r2.claim: The passage shifts from worldly punishment to their afterlife punishment; if the earlier threats referred to the afterlife, they summarize what this passage details.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p122/r2.anchor: فهذا انتقال إلى وصف ما يلقون من العذاب في الآخرة بعد أن ذكر عذابهم في الدنيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p122/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p122/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p122/r3.claim: The pronouns refer back to the polytheists who asked whether they would be resurrected after becoming dust and bones, not to the devils; the scene embeds a threat of punishment and regret.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p122/r3.anchor: وضمائر الغيبة عائدة إلى ما عادت عليه الضمائر السابقة من قوله { قالوا أإذا متنا وكنا ترابا وعظاما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p122/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p122/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p122/r4.claim: The plural imperative irjiʿūn addresses one person honorifically, a recognized Arabic form that uses masculine plural even when honoring a woman.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p122/r4.anchor: وضمير الجمع في { ارجعون } تعظيم للمخاطب . والخطاب بصيغة الجمع لقصد التعظيم طريقة عربية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p122/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p122/r5.speaker: العرجي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p122/r5.claim: Al-ʿArjī uses the plural suffix in siwākum when addressing one person honorifically.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p122/r5.anchor: قال العرجي : فإن شئتت حرمت النساء سواكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p122/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p122/r6.speaker: جعفر بن علبة الحارثي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p122/r6.claim: Jaʿfar ibn ʿUlba al-Ḥārithī likewise uses the honorific plural in baʿdakum.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p122/r6.anchor: وقال جعفر بن علبة الحارثي من شعراء الحماسة : فلا تحسبي أني تخشعت بعدكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p155#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p155#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p155#2/r1.claim: Hatta introduces the passage, though it might mark an endpoint with omitted material; the direct introductory reading better fits what is meant to be discussed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p155#2/r1.anchor: حتى في هذا الموضع حرف ابتداء ويحتمل أن تكون غاية مجردة بتقدير كلام محذوف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p155#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p155#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p155#2/r2.claim: The dead person is a disbeliever; irjiʿuni asks to return to worldly life, and the plural may magnify God's address or shift from calling God to addressing the punishing angels.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p155#2/r2.anchor: والضمير في قوله أحدهم للكفار، وقوله ارجعون معناه إلى الحياة الدنيا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p155#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p155#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p155#2/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says the dead person in this verse is a polytheist.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p155#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p155#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p155#2/r4.claim: A report to Aisha says the believer, when seeing death, chooses to go forward to God rather than return to the house of grief, while the unbeliever asks to return and do good.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p155#2/r4.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، لعائشة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p489#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p489#3/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p489#3/r1.claim: Although the dying person means return me, he says return us; Arabs use the plural about a person of great standing, as in God's words We give life and cause death.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p493/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p493/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p493/r1.claim: At death, unbelievers and those who neglected God's commands ask to return to worldly life so they can repair what they ruined; they are refused. The same plea appears in 63:10–11, 14:44, 7:53, 32:12, 6:27–28, 42:44, 40:11–12, and 35:37.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p493/r1.anchor: يخبر تعالى عن حال المحتضر عند الموت، من الكافرين أو المفرطين في أمر الله تعالى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p493/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p493/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p493/r2.claim: They are denied a return at the moment of death, at resurrection, during judgment before the Lord, and when shown the Fire; they remain amid the throes of Hell's punishment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p493/r2.anchor: فذكر تعالى أنهم يسألون الرجعة، فلا يجابون، عند الاحتضار، ويوم النشور ووقت العرض على الجبار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p493#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p493#2/r4.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p493#2/r4.claim: He portrays the dying person asking to return, then God answers that this is only a word he says.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p493#2/r4.anchor: محمد بن كعب القرظي: {حتى إذا جاء أحدهم الموت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p493#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p493#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p493#2/r6.claim: Qatāda transmits al-Alāʾ ibn Ziyād's advice to imagine death has arrived and one's request for reprieve was granted, then obey God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p493#2/r6.anchor: قال قتادة في قوله تعالى: {حتى إذا جاء أحدهم الموت}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p493#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p493#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p493#2/r7.claim: The unbeliever longs to return for obedience to God, not to rejoin family or tribe; the living should act on that wish.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p493#2/r7.anchor: والله ما تمنى أن يرجع إلى أهل ولا إلى عشيرة، ولكن تمنى أن يرجع فيعمل بطاعة الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p493#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p493#2/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p493#2/r8.claim: A dead unbeliever sees his place in the Fire, asks to return and repent, but is told his allotted life is over; the grave then constricts and its creatures torment him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p493#2/r8.anchor: عن أبي حازم، عن أبي هريرة قال: إذا وضع -يعني: الكافر-في قبره، فيرى مقعده من النار

JISHUMI:v7p5093/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5093/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5093/r3.claim: A report from the Prophet says that a believer asked by angels whether he wants to return to worldly sorrow declines and goes forward to God; the unbeliever asks for return as in these verses. No grading is stated.
JISHUMI:v7p5093/r3.anchor: وروي أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: إذا عاين المؤمن الملائكة فقالوا: نرجعك إلى دار الدنيا؟

JISHUMI:v7p5093/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5093/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5093/r4.claim: The dead ask to return and promise good works, showing their deeds and ability are their own; otherwise the request would be meaningless, refuting compulsion.
JISHUMI:v7p5093/r4.anchor: ويدل سؤالهم الرجعة ووعدهم بالعمل الصالح أن ذلك فعلهم، وأنهم قادرون على ذلك

JISHUMI:v7p5093/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5093/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5093/r5.claim: There is no return to worldly life after death, contrary to the Imamis, and resurrection will occur.
JISHUMI:v7p5093/r5.anchor: وتدل على أن لا رجعة إلى الدنيا، وذلك يبطل قول الإمامية. وتدل على البعث يوم القيامة

SAMIN-DURR:23:99/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:99/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:23:99/r1.claim: حتى may mark the endpoint of بما يصفون, with the following verse interrupting the clause for emphasis, or attach to وإنهم لكاذبون.

SAMIN-DURR:23:99/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:99/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:23:99/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya treats حتى as an inceptive particle or as a bare endpoint with omitted wording; he finds the first clearest because what follows is the intended point.

SAMIN-DURR:23:99/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:99/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:23:99/r3.claim: The Shaykh objects that inceptive حتى still carries an endpoint sense and that Ibn Atiyya failed to explain the omitted clause.

SAMIN-DURR:23:99/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:99/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:23:99/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqa describes حتى as an endpoint with the force of coordination.

SAMIN-DURR:23:99/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:99/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:23:99/r5.claim: The Shaykh proposes an omitted prior clause implied by context, ending at حتى إذا جاء; a poem shows the endpoint after an omitted broad subject.
SAMIN-DURR:23:99/r5.anchor: والذي يظهر لي أن قبلها جملة محذوفة

SAMIN-DURR:23:99#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:99#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:99#2/r1.claim: ارجعون may be a plural of reverence, the strongest explanation; poetic address in the plural rebuts Ibn Malik's claim that none permits this prayer form.
SAMIN-DURR:23:99#2/r1.anchor: أجودها: أنه على سبيل التعظيم كقول الشاعر:

SAMIN-DURR:23:99#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:99#2/r2.speaker: ابن مالك
SAMIN-DURR:23:99#2/r2.claim: Ibn Malik says he knows no one who permits a supplicant to say يا رحيمون, to avoid suggesting plurality in God; the author answers that scripture uses such forms for reverence.
SAMIN-DURR:23:99#2/r2.anchor: إنه لم يعلم أحدا أجاز للداعي يقول:

SAMIN-DURR:23:99#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:99#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:99#2/r3.claim: The author rejects Ibn Malik's restriction because God uses plural forms for reverence in several scriptural passages.
SAMIN-DURR:23:99#2/r3.anchor: وقد أخبر تعالى عن نفسه بهذه الصيغة وشبهها للتعظيم في غير موضع من كتابه الكريم

SAMIN-DURR:23:99#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:99#2/r4.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:23:99#2/r4.claim: Another parse has the speaker call on his Lord, then address the Lord's angels with ارجعون, deleting an understood إضافة such as يا ملائكة ربي and shifting the pronoun as in 7:4.
SAMIN-DURR:23:99#2/r4.anchor: أنه نادى ربه، ثم خاطب ملائكة ربه بقوله:

SAMIN-DURR:23:99#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:99#2/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:23:99#2/r5.claim: Abu al-Baqa says the plural may repeat the command: ارجعون three times, like the doubled command ألقيا and the poem قفا نبك.
SAMIN-DURR:23:99#2/r5.anchor: أن ذلك يدل على تكرير الفعل، كأنه قال:

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p205/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p205/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p205/r2.claim: Plural address to God is for exaltation, as in the cited poetic forms of address.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p205/r2.anchor: خطاب الله بلفظ الجمع للتعظيم ، كقوله : فإن شئت حرمت النساء سواكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p205/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p205/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p205/r3.claim: At death, seeing the truth brings remorse for neglected faith and good works, so the dying person asks to return and do what was left of faith.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p205/r3.anchor: إذا أيقن بالموت واطلع على حقيقة الأمر ، أدركته الحسرة على ما فرط فيه من الإيمان

MUQATIL:23:91-100/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:91-100/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:91-100/r8.claim: At death the unbeliever sees his sins as the Angel of Death takes him; struck by disgrace, he asks to return to worldly life and do the good he left behind, meaning faith.
MUQATIL:23:91-100/r8.anchor: حين يعاين ملك الموت يؤخذ بلسانه، فينظر إلى سيئاته قبل الموت،

NASAFI-FULL:v3p130#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p130#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p130#5/r1.claim: The clause continues either the description of persistent association with God or of persistent ill-repute, ending when death arrives; the intervening account urges restraint from revenge.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p130#5/r1.anchor: لا يزالون يشركون إلى وقت مجئ الموت أو لا يزالون على سوء الذكر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p130#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p130#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p130#5/r2.claim: “My Lord, return me” addresses God in the plural as an honorific, like addressing kings.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p130#5/r2.anchor: أى ردونى إلى الدنيا خاطب الله بلفظ الجمع للتعظيم كخطاب الملوك

QURTUBI-FULL:23:99-100/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:99-100/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:99-100/r1.claim: The discussion returns to idolaters who persist in denying resurrection; when death comes they see the angels taking their souls and realize their error, as in the account of angels seizing disbelievers.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:99-100/r1.anchor: تيقن ضلالته وعاين الملائكة التي تقبض روحه كما قال تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:23:99-100/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:99-100/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:99-100/r2.claim: They ask to be returned so they can do the good they neglected; the words may have been spoken only inwardly.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:99-100/r2.anchor: تمنى الرجعة كي يعمل صالحا فيما ترك

QURTUBI-FULL:23:99-100/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:99-100/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:99-100/r3.claim: The plural imperative addressing God may magnify the addressee; Ibn Jurayj says they first call on God, then address the angels to return them to this world.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:99-100/r3.anchor: وقيل: استغاثوا بالله عز وجل أولا، فقال قائلهم: رب، ثم رجع إلى مخاطبة الملائكة

QURTUBI-FULL:23:99-100/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:99-100/r4.speaker: المزني
QURTUBI-FULL:23:99-100/r4.claim: Another explanation takes irjiʿūn as repetition meaning return me again and again, like the reading of al-Muzani’s explanation of the command to throw into Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:99-100/r4.anchor: على جهة التكرير أي ارجعني ارجعني ارجعني وهكذا

QURTUBI-FULL:23:99-100/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:99-100/r5.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:23:99-100/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says the request is made by the people of shirk; the author adds that believers also ask for return, as discussed at the end of al-Munafiqun.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:99-100/r5.anchor: قال الضحاك: المراد به أهل الشرك. قلت: ليس سؤال الرجعة مختصا بالكافر

QURTUBI-FULL:23:99-100/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:99-100/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:99-100/r6.claim: The request indicates that before death people know with certainty whether they belong to God’s allies or enemies, since otherwise they would not ask to return.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:99-100/r6.anchor: ودلت الآية على أن أحدا لا يموت حتى يعرف اضطرارا أهو من أولياء الله أم من أعداء الله

RAZI-FULL:v23p103/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p103/r7.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v23p103/r7.claim: Al-Kashshaf connects “until” to the earlier description: their bad mention continues until death; the intervening verse emphasizes turning away from them with God's help against Satan.
RAZI-FULL:v23p103/r7.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) حتى متعلق بيصفون

RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says one who neglected charity and pilgrimage asks to return at death; when challenged that only disbelievers ask, he cites the warning to spend before death.
RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r1.anchor: قال الضحاك كنت جالسا عند ابن عباس

RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r2.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r2.claim: The Prophet says that, as death approaches, a person sees all the rights he had withheld brought before him and asks to return and act righteously.
RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r2.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r3.claim: The request is by disbelievers: believers who see their place in Paradise would not wish for more, while the least rewarded would otherwise grieve over higher ranks.
RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r3.anchor: والأقرب هو الأول إذا عرف المؤمن منزلته في الجنة فإذا شاهدها لا يتمنى أكثر منها

RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r4.claim: The cited warning to spend before death describes worldly life, not the state of reward, so it does not overturn the preferred reading.
RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r4.anchor: فهو إخبار عن حال الحياة في الدنيا لا عن حال الثواب فلا يلزم على ما ذكرنا

RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r5.claim: Most interpreters place the request at the moment of death's direct apprehension, when the person is compelled to recognize God and his disobedience.
RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r5.anchor: فالأكثرون على أنه يسأل في حال المعاينة لأنه عندها يضطر إلى معرفة الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r6.claim: Others place the request when the condemned see Hell in the afterlife, drawing on other descriptions of Hell's inhabitants asking to return.
RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون بل يقول ذلك عند معاينة النار في الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r7.claim: The verse itself attaches the request to death's arrival, so there is no reason to abandon that apparent timing, even if they later ask again.
RAZI-FULL:v23p104/r7.anchor: فعلق قولهم هذا بحال حضور الموت وهو حال المعاينة فلا وجه لترك هذا الظاهر

RAZI-FULL:v23p104#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p104#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p104#2/r1.claim: Some take the plural “return me” as addressing the angels who seize souls; on this view “Lord” is an oath invoking the Lord's right.
RAZI-FULL:v23p104#2/r1.anchor: الملائكة الذين يقبضون الأرواح وهم جماعة

RAZI-FULL:v23p104#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p104#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p104#2/r2.claim: Others take the addressee to be God, with the plural expressing reverence; a poet's plural address illustrates this form.
RAZI-FULL:v23p104#2/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون بل المراد هو الله تعالى لأن قوله رب بمنزلة أن يقول يا رب

RAZI-FULL:v23p104#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p104#2/r3.speaker: الشاعر
RAZI-FULL:v23p104#2/r3.claim: An anonymous poetic line supplies an example of plural address used for a singular addressee as a form of reverence.
RAZI-FULL:v23p104#2/r3.anchor:
قال الشاعر :
فإن شئت حرمت النساء سواكم

RAZI-FULL:v23p104#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p104#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p104#2/r4.claim: A person may ask for a return even while knowing it cannot occur; such supplication is permissible, and the wish may be a mere hope.
RAZI-FULL:v23p104#2/r4.anchor: فلا يمتنع أن يسألوه لأن الاستعانة بهذا الجنس من المسألة تحسن وإن علم أنه لا يقع

ASAD-NOTES:23:99#n59/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:99#n59/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:23:99#n59/r1.claim: This passage connects with verses 74 and 90 above.

ASAD-NOTES:23:99#n60/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:99#n60/r1.speaker: most commentators
ASAD-NOTES:23:99#n60/r1.claim: Most commentators take the plural command to return as a reverential form of address.
ASAD-NOTES:23:99#n60/r1.anchor: Most of the commentators regard the plural form of address

ASAD-NOTES:23:99#n60/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:99#n60/r2.speaker: Baydawi
ASAD-NOTES:23:99#n60/r2.claim: Baydawi argues from pre-Islamic poetry that the plural is an emphatic repetition of the singular, which Asad reflects by repeating the plea.
ASAD-NOTES:23:99#n60/r2.anchor: Baydawi suggests - on the strength of examples from pre-islamic poetry - that this plural form

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.claim: The opposition of affluent and powerful people to prophets recurs throughout this surah, as elsewhere in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.anchor: The opposition to prophets by the affluent and powerful is a recurrent theme in this sūrah

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.claim: The conclusion warns that disbelievers facing their perdition will wish to return to do good instead of evil, but it will be too late.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.anchor: will desire to go back to the world in order to do good instead of evil, though it will be too late for them (vv.99–118)

STUDYQURAN:23:99/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:99/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:99/r1.claim: The opening 'Till' continues the rejection recounted in 23:83: disbelievers persist in it until death comes.
STUDYQURAN:23:99/r1.anchor: Till is understood to follow the end of v. 83, which recounts the dismissive words of the disbelievers

STUDYQURAN:23:99/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:99/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:99/r2.claim: Other verses likewise portray the dead seeking return so they may give charity or do righteous deeds.
STUDYQURAN:23:99/r2.anchor: The desire of those who have died to return to the world is also mentioned vividly in 32:12

STUDYQURAN:23:99/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:99/r3.speaker: Some commentators
STUDYQURAN:23:99/r3.claim: Some commentators place the plea before death: after addressing God, the dying person asks the soul-taking angels to return him.
STUDYQURAN:23:99/r3.anchor: Some commentators understand the plea for return in this verse

STUDYQURAN:23:99/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:99/r4.speaker: Others (R)
STUDYQURAN:23:99/r4.claim: Other commentators place the request after death, when the person has seen the Fire.
STUDYQURAN:23:99/r4.anchor: Others understand this request to be spoken after death, after beholding the Fire (R)

TAB-FULL:v17p107/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p107/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p107/r1.claim: At death the polytheist regrets neglected obedience and asks to return to worldly life so he can do the righteous deeds he abandoned.
TAB-FULL:v17p107/r1.anchor: لعظيم ما يعاين مما يقدم عليه من عذاب الله تندما على ما فات، وتلهفا على ما فرط فيه

TAB-FULL:v17p107/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p107/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v17p107/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says the plea occurs as worldly life ends and the person sees the afterlife, before tasting death.
TAB-FULL:v17p107/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {رب ارجعون} [المؤمنون: 99] قال: هذه في الحياة الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v17p107/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p107/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v17p107/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says those asking “My Lord, return me” are the people of shirk.
TAB-FULL:v17p107/r5.anchor: سمعت أبا معاذ يقول: أخبرنا عبيد قال: سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله: {حتى إذا جاء أحدهم الموت قال رب ارجعون} [المؤمنون: 99] «يعني أهل الشرك»

TAB-FULL:v17p107/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p107/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p107/r6.claim: The plea begins by addressing God, then shifts to the plural “return me,” because the request is directed to the angels who take the soul.
TAB-FULL:v17p107/r6.anchor: مسألة القوم الرد إلى الدنيا إنما كانت منهم للملائكة الذين يقبضون روحهم

TAB-FULL:v17p107/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p107/r7.speaker: بعض نحويي الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v17p107/r7.claim: A Kufan grammarian explains the plural form as following the Qur'anic pattern in which God describes himself with plural wording, as in “I created you.”
TAB-FULL:v17p107/r7.anchor: وكان بعض نحويي الكوفة يقول: قيل ذلك كذلك، لأنه مما جرى على وصف الله نفسه

TABRISI:23:96-100/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:96-100/r6.speaker: ابن جرير
TABRISI:23:96-100/r6.claim: The plural ‘return me’ may first address God, then turn to the angels with the request to send the dying person back to worldly life.
TABRISI:23:96-100/r6.anchor: استغاثوا أولا بالله ثم رجعوا إلى مسائلة الملائكة

TABRISI:23:96-100/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:96-100/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:96-100/r7.claim: Another explanation treats the plural as the Arabs' customary honorific form of address; when asked, al-Khalil said he did not know its precise meaning.
TABRISI:23:96-100/r7.anchor: أنه على عادة العرب في تعظيم المخاطب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p191/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p191/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p191/r1.claim: The dying person in al-Mu'minun asks to do righteous work, not specifically to give charity; this shows righteousness is the basis of salvation outside a passage about wealth.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p191/r1.anchor: فإنه ذكر الصلاح ولم يذكر الصدقة، لأن الآية لم تقع في سياق الكلام على الأموال وإنفاقها

THALABI:v7p55/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p55/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p55/r1.claim: The dying person is one of the polytheists, who sees the afterlife as worldly life ends, before tasting death.
THALABI:v7p55/r1.anchor: يعني هؤلاء المشركين، وذلك حين ينقطع عن الدنيا ويعاين الآخرة قبل أن يذوق الموت

THALABI:v7p55/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p55/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p55/r2.claim: The singular person says ارجعون using a majestic plural form, like the divine نحن.

THALABI:v7p55/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p55/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p55/r3.claim: Another explanation is that he first calls on God, then addresses the angels who are taking his soul to ask for return.
THALABI:v7p55/r3.anchor: إنما كانت منهم للملائكة الذين يقبضون روحه

THALABI:v7p55/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p55/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p55/r4.claim: He asks to return so he can do righteous deeds among what he left behind; كلا rebukes him and denies the request.
THALABI:v7p55/r4.anchor: لعلي أعمل صالحا فيما تركت صنعت كلا أي لا يرجع إليها

THALABI:v7p55/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p55/r5.speaker: عائشة
THALABI:v7p55/r5.claim: The Prophet says a believer offered return to the world rejects it as a place of worries, while the unbeliever asks to return.
THALABI:v7p55/r5.anchor: إذا عاين المؤمن الملائكة قالوا: نرجعك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r1.claim: Those who denied resurrection ask to return to worldly life when they see death approaching.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r1.anchor: أن هؤلاء الذين ذكروا قبل هذا الموضع ودفعوا البعث يسألون المرجع إلى الدنيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r2.claim: Muqatil says the person who asks to return is a disbeliever.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r3.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r3.claim: They explain “death came” as meaning the Angel of Death came.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r3.anchor: قال الكلبي ومقاتل (¬5): يعني ملك الموت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r4.speaker: غيرهما
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r4.claim: Others take “death” to mean its causes and early signs, as in the verse about death coming from every direction.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r4.anchor: وقال غيرهما: يعني (¬6) أسباب الموت ومقدماته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r5.speaker: ابن عباس والمفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r5.claim: “My Lord, send me back” means return me to worldly life.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس والمفسرون: يريد إلى الدنيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r6.speaker: الفراء والزجاج وجميع أصحاب العربية
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r6.claim: The plural imperative “send me back” addresses God alone; Arabic uses a plural form for a majestic speaker, as in God's “We give life and cause death.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r6.anchor: قال الفراء، والزجاج، وجميع أصحاب العربية: قوله: {ارجعون} وهو يريد الله -عز وجل- وحده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the dying person first calls on God and then turns to the angels to ask for return.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r7.anchor: وروي عن ابن جريج أنه قال -في هذه الآية-: إنهم استغاثوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r8.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r8.claim: Al-Mubarrad chooses the angels as the addressees of “send me back,” after the person first appeals to God; Arabic can shift addressees mid-speech, as in lines by al-Ahwas and al-Nabigha addressing a house before its owner.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p60/r8.anchor: واختار المبرد هذا الوجه فقال: {ارجعون} خطاب للملائكة بعد أن قال: رب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:96-101/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:96-101/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:96-101/r4.claim: When death comes, the person asks God to return him to worldly life.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:96-101/r4.anchor: { رب ارجعون } أي: ارددني إلى الدنيا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p415/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p415/r1.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p415/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says anyone without God's friendship asks to return at death once the Fire becomes clear, even someone mute who never spoke; those nearby do not hear the request.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p415/r1.anchor: قال الحسن: ليس أحد من خلق الله ليس لله بولي إلا وهو يسأل الله الرجعة إلى الدنيا عند الموت

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p415/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p415/r3.speaker: رسول الله
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p415/r3.claim: A report from an unnamed man of Banū Ḥāritha says a dying person sees what had kept him from his obligations placed before him, prompting the plea to return; versions place these things before him or between his eyes.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p415/r3.anchor: عن رجل من بني حارثة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إذا حضر الإنسان الموت جمع كل شيء له كان يمنعه من الحق

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p415/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p415/r4.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p415/r4.claim: Al-Suddī says a dying unbeliever sees few good deeds and many bad ones, sees the Angel of Death, and wishes to return, then God says he will not return; descendants do not hear the utterance.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p415/r4.anchor: قال يحيى: وأخبرني رجل من أهل الكوفة عن السدي قال: إن الكافر إذا نزل به الموت وعاين حسناته قليلة وسيئاته كثيرة،

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:99/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:99/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:99/r1.claim: ‘They’ especially means unbelievers who deny resurrection; only after death, when worldly ties and desires end, do they recognize their mistake and express despair and regret.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:99/r1.anchor: “Onlar”dan maksat, özellikle öldükten sonra tekrar dirilmenin imkânsız olduğunu savunan inkârcılardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:99/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:99/r2.speaker: Fahreddin er-Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:99/r2.claim: Razi says they cry out at death—or, in a weak view, on seeing their place in Hell—knowing return is impossible but grieving that they died unbelievers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:99/r2.anchor: Fahreddin er-Râzî’ye göre böyleleri, ölümleri esnasında (veya zayıf bir görüşe göre âhirette cehennemdeki yerlerini görünce)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:99/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:99/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:99/r3.claim: The verses explicitly reject reincarnation, an idea traced to ancient Indian religions and Plato: if souls could migrate between bodies until purified, God would not refuse the sinners’ request to return and correct their lives.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:99/r3.anchor: 99-100. âyetler, temeli eski Hint dinlerine ve Eflâtun felsefesine kadar uzanan, zaman zaman günümüzde bile bazı kişiler ve sözde ilim adamları tarafından savunulan reenkarnasyon (tenâsüh) inancını açıkça reddetmektedir.

ITQAN:v3p104/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p104/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p104/r1.claim: The plural imperative ارجعون is used for one speaker's request, meaning ارجعني.
ITQAN:v3p104/r1.anchor: أي أرجعني وجعل منه ابن فارس

ITQAN:v3p89/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p89/r10.speaker: بعضهم
ITQAN:v3p89/r10.claim: Some read the plural “return me” as a plural form of address for the singular request “My Lord, return me.”
ITQAN:v3p89/r10.anchor: وجعل منه بعضهم ﴿ قال رب ارجعون ﴾ أي ارجعني

ITQAN:v3p89/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p89/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p89/r11.claim: An alternative parses “Lord” as addressed to God and “return me” as addressed to the angels.
ITQAN:v3p89/r11.anchor: وقيل ( رب ) خطاب له تعالى و ( ارجعون ) للملائكة

ITQAN:v3p89/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p89/r12.speaker: السهيلي
ITQAN:v3p89/r12.claim: Al-Suhaylī says a dying person speaks incoherently when beset by devils and the guards of punishment.
ITQAN:v3p89/r12.anchor: وقال السهيلي هو قول من حضرته الشياطين وزبانية العذاب

DAMGHANI:v1p191/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p191/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p191/r3.claim: Rajaʿa can mean send back or return; the source groups the plea to be sent back with returning to one's mother and looking again.
DAMGHANI:v1p191/r3.anchor: " قال رب ارجعون " أي ردوني كقوله تعالى في سورة طه " فرجعناك إلى أمك "

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p115/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p115/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p115/r1.claim: Death receives doubled emphasis in al-Muʾminūn because the sūra repeatedly depicts death and mortality, whereas al-Zumar mentions death only twice.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p115/r1.anchor: لقد أكد الموت في آية (المؤمنون) بإن واللام في حين أكده في الزمر بإن وحدها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p613/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p613/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p613/r1.claim: He distinguishes presence or witnessing (حضور) from coming, which is movement between places; Qur’anic examples use both for death and for arriving events.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p613/r1.anchor: أما المجيء فهو الإنتقال من مكان إلى مكان، فالحضور إذن غير المجيء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p613/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p613/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p613/r2.claim: He describes God as present everywhere and presents this as evidence of His existence everywhere.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p613/r2.anchor: ولهذا نقول الله حاضر في كل مكان دليل وجوده في كل مكان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p614/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p614/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p614/r3.claim: جاء الموت is used when discussing death itself or the dying person's condition, as in the dying person who asks to return and do good.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p614/r3.anchor: أما مجيء الموت في القرآن فيستعمل في الكلام عن الموت نفسه أو أحوال الناس في الموت كما في آية سورة المؤمنون

NASHR:v1p382#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p382#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p382#2/r3.claim: The two-fatḥa class contains 16 forms across 29 places; the list includes جاء أحد منكم, جاء أجلهم, جاء أمرنا, جاء آل, جاء أحدهم, and شاء أنشره.
NASHR:v1p382#2/r3.anchor: وأما المتفقتان فتحا، ففي ستة عشر لفظا في تسعة وعشرين موضعا

NASHR:v2p101/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p101/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p101/r1.claim: Readers agree on lightening rāʾ when it is final in connected recitation, and on lightening it initially or medially when it carries kasra.
NASHR:v2p101/r1.anchor: القراء على ترقيق هذه الراءات المتطرفات وصلا كما أنهم أجمعوا على ترقيقها مبتدأة ومتوسطة إذا كانت مكسورة

NASHR:v2p101/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p101/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p101/r4.claim: Sākin rāʾ is emphatic after fatḥa or ḍamma; examples after kasra also remain emphatic when the kasra is incidental or the rāʾ’s underlying quality is emphatic.
NASHR:v2p101/r4.anchor: فهي مفخمة على كل حال لوقوعها بعد ضم ولكون الكسرة عارضة

NASHR:v2p101/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p101/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p101/r5.claim: In ارجعي and ارجعون, the preceding kasra is incidental, so the rāʾ remains emphatic; the author gives the same rule for ارجعوا and related forms.
NASHR:v2p101/r5.anchor: فهي أيضا في ذلك مفخمة لعروض الكسر قبلها وكون الراء في ذلك أصلها التفخيم

NASHR:v2p101/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p101/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p101/r6.claim: Medial sākin rāʾ is emphatic after fatḥa, ḍamma, or kasra in the examples; قرية, مريم, and المرء are exceptions, and named authorities specify lightening قرية and مريم for all readers.
NASHR:v2p101/r6.anchor: فأما قرية حيث وقعت ومريم فنص على الترقيق فيهما لجميع القراء

NASHR:v2p329#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p329#2/r6.speaker: يعقوب
NASHR:v2p329#2/r6.claim: Yaqub affirms the six listed extra yāʾs in both connected and pause forms: بما كذبون twice, فاتقون, أن يحضرون, رب ارجعون, and ولا تكلمون.

NASHR:v1p388/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p388/r1.speaker: مكي، والمهدوي، وابن سفيان، وصاحب العنوان
NASHR:v1p388/r1.claim: Makki, al-Mahdawi, Ibn Sufyan, and the author of al-Unwan choose easing; the author also names the Rawda, Mubhij, two Ghayas, Talkhis, and others. Al-Tajrid’s author says he read it from al-Farisi and Abd al-Baqi.
NASHR:v1p388/r1.anchor: وبالتسهيل قطع مكي، والمهدوي، وابن سفيان

NASHR:v1p388/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p388/r2.speaker: أصحاب التذكرة والتيسير والكافي والشاطبية والتجريد
NASHR:v1p388/r2.claim: Al-Tadhkira, al-Taysir, al-Kafi, al-Shatibiyya, Talkhis al-Ibarat, and al-Tajrid report both easing and full pronunciation.
NASHR:v1p388/r2.anchor: ونص على الوجهين في " التذكرة "، و " التيسير "

NASHR:v1p388/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p388/r3.speaker: ابن شريح
NASHR:v1p388/r3.claim: Ibn Shurayh’s easing like wāw is rejected by the author as unsupported and impossible without an impermissible conversion or rounding of the hamza’s kasra.
NASHR:v1p388/r3.anchor: وقد أبعد وأغرب ابن شريح في كافيه، حيث حكى تسهيلها كالواو

NASHR:v1p388/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p388/r4.speaker: ابن عامر، وعاصم، وحمزة، والكسائي، وخلف، وروح
NASHR:v1p388/r4.claim: Ibn Amir, Asim, Hamza, al-Kisai, Khalaf, and Rawh fully pronounce both hamzas in all five categories; Ibn Mihran alone reports easing for Rawh, like Ruways and the group.
NASHR:v1p388/r4.anchor: وقرأ الباقون وهم ابن عامر، وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي وخلف، وروح بتحقيق الهمزتين جميعا

NASHR:v1p388/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p388/r5.speaker: أبو الطيب بن غلبون، وأبو الحسن الحمامي
NASHR:v1p388/r5.claim: Ibn Ghalbun and al-Hammami say Abu Amr drops the second hamza, following al-Khalil and grammarians; most performance authorities say he drops the first, which the author chooses by analogy of like letters. This changes whether preceding madd is connected or separate.
NASHR:v1p388/r5.anchor: ذهب أبو الطيب بن غلبون فيما حكاه عنه صاحب " التجريد "

NASHR:v1p388/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p388/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p388/r6.claim: When the second like hamza becomes a madd letter and a consonant follows, its length increases to resolve two adjacent sukūns; without a following consonant it stays at the length of a madd letter.
NASHR:v1p388/r6.anchor: زيد في مد حرف المد المبدل لالتقاء الساكنين، فإن لم يكن بعده ساكن لم يزد

NASHR:v1p388/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p388/r7.speaker: أصحاب الداني
NASHR:v1p388/r7.claim: For the two open hamzas in جاء آل لوط and جاء آل فرعون, al-Dani reports disagreement over replacing the second or easing it because an alif follows; some reject replacement to avoid two consecutive alifs.
NASHR:v1p388/r7.anchor: قال الداني: اختلف أصحابنا في ذلك، فقال بعضهم: لا يبدلها فيهما
